sidebar.defaultNote: The Default account is your normal Claude Code login on this Mac; you cannot log out of it here.
sidebar.resumeTitle: When the app starts, each project continues its last Claude session (claude --continue)
sidebar.resumeWorkTitle: If the app closed while Claude was working (an update, a restart, a crash), that project starts right away when the app opens again and Claude is told to check what was finished and carry on. Needs "Continue last session".
sidebar.resumeUnfinishedTitle: Checks every project: a Claude whose last turn did not finish (the app restarted or an update came while it worked, the session ended, a crash) is told to check what was finished and carry on. A stopped or sleeping one starts with its session; an idle one gets the message typed in. Busy ones, and ones with unsent text, are left alone.
sidebar.resumeUnfinishedSkipped: Left alone (unsent text in its input): {names}
sidebar.managerTitle: The boss splits the work across agents, keeps going until the tasks are done and stops only for what needs you (approvals, logins, your decisions). Applies to Claude sessions started afterwards.
sidebar.reloadMcpTitle: When the MCP servers a running Claude would get change (claude mcp add/remove, an edited .mcp.json, an approval, a project added), it restarts in the same conversation as soon as it is idle: not while it works, runs agents or background shells, waits for an approval or has unsent text in its prompt.
sidebar.shareMcpTitle: Each project's Claude also gets the MCP servers the other projects in the office have (their local and approved .mcp.json servers, with their tokens), so you can work on one project from another's tab. A server whose name is already taken with another setup gets the project's name added (server-project). Applies to Claude sessions started afterwards.
sidebar.shareDefault: Use Default's plugins, skills and MCP servers
sidebar.shareDefaultTitle: Plugins, personal skills, agents, commands, output styles, MCP servers (with their tokens) and CLAUDE.md you installed for the Default account (~/.claude) are available in this account too. This account's own login, settings and claude.ai-synced skills stay its own. Applies when this account's Claude sessions start next.
sidebar.sleepTitle: Saves memory: a project starts its Claude when first opened, and a background Claude that has been idle this long is ended and continues its session (claude --resume) when you open the project again. Never while it works, waits for approval, runs agents, background shells or scheduled tasks, or has unsent text.
sidebar.themeAutoTitle: Each project gets its own office colors (or a theme from your themes.json whose match fits its folder name)
sidebar.themeClassicTitle: Classic: red brick and warm wood, the default office
sidebar.themeForestTitle: Forest: green walls, green carpet and leafy accents
sidebar.splitTitle: Drag to resize · double-click to reset
sidebar.accountTitle: Claude account used in this project (changing it restarts Claude)
sidebar.projectManagerTitle: How this project's boss works: Global follows the Manager mode setting; Delegates splits the work across agents; Does it itself works without agents. Either way it keeps going until the work is done. Applies when the project's Claude starts next (idle tabs restart now).
sidebar.agentModelTitle: The model this project's agents (subagents) run on. Auto lets the boss pick per agent: Haiku for searches, Sonnet for routine edits, tests and builds, its own model for design, hard debugging and reviews. Sonnet, Haiku or Opus runs every agent on that model. Applies when the project's Claude starts next (idle tabs restart now).
sidebar.contextCapTitle: How large this project's conversations may grow before Claude summarizes them (auto-compact), for the boss and its agents. Every step re-reads the whole conversation, so a lower cap means Claude summarizes earlier, each step re-reads less and the work costs less. The trade-off: details of earlier work are kept only as a summary. Auto uses Claude Code's own limit (up to 1M tokens on a 1M model). Applies when the project's Claude starts next (idle tabs restart now).
sidebar.savingsTitle: Cuts token use, mostly from agents (subagents). Normal: an agent is told to wrap up and report briefly after 40 tool calls; Bash output is kept to 15,000 characters and MCP results to 15,000 tokens (longer output goes to a file Claude can read). Strict: the reminder comes after 25 calls, calls past 50 are refused so the agent answers, and output is kept to 8,000. Off changes nothing. Applies when the project's Claude starts next (idle tabs restart now).

sidebar.fallback: Backup account at the usage limit
sidebar.fallbackTitle: When a project's account reaches its usage limit, the project moves to its backup account (chosen in the project's row) and every tab resumes its own conversation there; tabs stopped by the limit carry on with their work. Once the first account's limit resets and the tabs are idle, the project moves back. A backup that is not logged in or is at its limit too is skipped.
sidebar.backupTitle: The account this project continues on when its own account reaches the usage limit. Any free account picks another logged-in account that still has quota. Needs “Backup account at the usage limit” (on by default).
sidebar.onBackupTitle: Moved here when {home} reached its usage limit. It goes back to {home} once that limit resets and every tab is idle.

usage.title: Token usage
usage.usdTitle: Estimated at API list prices, not a bill: a Pro or Max plan pays a flat fee.

usage.fullPriceTitle: Each kind is weighted by its price relative to input tokens: input 1×, cache write 1.25× (kept 5 minutes) or 2× (kept 1 hour), cache read 0.1× (less on some models), output 5×.

kindTitle.output: What the model wrote (text, code, tool calls): 5× the input price
kindTitle.input: New context that was not in the cache: the full input price
kindTitle.write: Context stored in the prompt cache: 1.25× the input price when kept 5 minutes, 2× when kept 1 hour
kindTitle.read: Context the model had already seen, served from the cache: a tenth of the input price

usage.noteRead: A cache read is context the model has already seen; it costs a tenth of the full price.
usage.noteEstimate: $ is an estimate at API list prices, not a bill.
